L00008: L00009: ## 📰 News L00010: L00011: - **2025-11-06**: We apologize for the recent Snowflake login and credential issues caused by Snowflake’s password & MFA policy upgrade. Both **Web UI login** and **Python credential access** behaviors have changed. L00012: Please **carefully review the updated Snowflake guideline** before continuing: L00013: https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/blob/main/assets/Snowflake_Guideline.md L00014: Thank you for your patience and understanding! L00015: L00016: - **2025-10-29**: Major update! L00017: 1. We fixed the evaluation-suite issue, so scores are now more accurate and stable. We also refreshed the affected methods on the [leaderboard](https://spider2-sql.github.io/). L00018: 2. If you are willing to cover the Snowflake hosting cost (spider2-snow is free by default, but queries are queued), we can share the Spider2 Snowflake data directly to your own Snowflake project. See [Spider2_Data_Host.md](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/blob/main/assets/Spider2_Data_Host.md) for details. L00019: 3. If you run into MF2A connection errors—meaning your credentials cannot access the Snowflake warehouse—check. Please see [Snowflake Guideline](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/blob/main/assets/Snowflake_Guideline.md). L00020: L00021: L00022: - **2025-07-13**: We update [`spider2-snow.jsonl`](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/blob/main/spider2-snow/spider2-snow.jsonl) to resolve ambiguities, with the previous version renamed to [`spider2-snow-0713.jsonl`](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/blob/main/spider2-snow/spider2-snow-0713.jsonl) for reference. L00023: L00024: - **2025-06-10**: We implemented a [tool-call-based Spider-Agent](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/tree/main/methods/spider-agent-tc) for Spider 2.0-Snow that requires no Docker and significantly improves runtime performance. L00025: L00026: - **2025-05-22**: We have created a new task setting, `Spider2-DBT`, and removed the original Spider2 setting. [spider2-dbt](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/tree/main/spider2-dbt) consists of only 68 tasks, enabling quick and smooth benchmarking with [spider-agent-dbt](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/tree/main/methods/spider-agent-dbt). It is a comprehensive, repository-level text-to-SQL task. L00027: L00028: - **2025-04-20**: We provide the [ground-truth tables](https://github.com/xlang-ai/Spider2/tree/main/methods/gold-tables) for spider2-lite and spider2-snow to help quick benchmarking and analysis. However, when using this setting, you must indicate that you are using `oracle tables`. L00029: L00030: - **2025-01-10**: Please refer to the [data update log](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a69mxO7m1nMndXp8H_-aggvYDbcbiS3rV9GPXEw-DeM/edit?usp=sharing) to track changes in the evaluation examples. The [leaderboard](https://spider2-sql.github.io/) results will also change dynamically accordingly. L00031: L00032: L00035: L00036: - **2024-12-24**: Considering the many evaluation requirements, we have decided to **release all examples and gold answers for self-evaluation**. However, only a small amount of gold SQL is available. The leaderboard is still active. To have your method officially validated and upload your scores to the leaderboard, please follow the [submission guidance](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sCobAqJZcko-Vl3biOycwvCIR7kTwBPrhsgVfvaX1Fg/edit?usp=sharing). L00011: def string_match(pred, gold, conj="or", exclude=[]):
L00012:     """
L00013: 
L00014:     Parameters:
L00015:     - pred (str): The string in which to search for substrings.
L00016:     - gold (list of str): A list of strings to be checked within the pred string.
L00017:     - conj (str): The conjunction to use for matching ('and' or 'or'). Defaults to 'or'. 
L00018:     - exclude (list of str): some string can't exist in the answer.
L00019: 
L00020:     Returns:
L00021:     - int: Returns 1 if the condition specified by 'conj' is met, otherwise returns 0.
L00022: 
L00023:     """
L00024:     
L00025:     if not isinstance(gold, list):
L00026:         gold = [gold]
L00027:     
L00028:     pred_lower = pred.lower()
L00029:     gold_lower = [sub.lower() for sub in gold]
L00030:     exclude_lower = [sub.lower() for sub in exclude]
L00031: 
L00032:     if any(sub in pred_lower for sub in exclude_lower):
L00033:         return 0  # Return 0 if any excluded items are found
L00034:     
L00035:     if conj == "or":
L00036:         # Check if any of the strings in 'gold_lower' are in 'pred_lower'
L00037:         return 1 if any(sub in pred_lower for sub in gold_lower) else 0
L00038:     elif conj == "and":
L00039:         # Check if all of the strings in 'gold_lower' are in 'pred_lower'
L00040:         return 1 if all(sub in pred_lower for sub in gold_lower) else 0
L00041:     else:
L00042:         raise ValueError("Invalid value for 'conj'. Choose 'and' or 'or'.")
L00043:

L00046: def number_match(pred, gold, percentage=False, precision=4, conj="or"):
L00047:     """
L00048:     Parameters:
L00049:     - pred (str): The string in which to search for substrings.
L00050:     - gold (list[str|float] of str): A list of string/numbers to be checked within the pred string.
L00051:     - percentage (bool): default false. if the gold answer is related with "percentage", set it as true to make the evaluation robust.
L00052:     - precision: Decimal places
L00053:     - conj (str): The conjunction to use for matching ('and' or 'or'). Defaults to 'or'. Most time is 'or'
L00054:     
L00055:     """
L00056:     
L00057:     import regex
L00058: 
L00059:     def extract_numbers(input_string):
L00060:         """
L00061:         Extracts all numbers from a given string including integers, floating-point numbers,
L00062:         numbers with commas, and percentages, returning them as a list of strings in their
L00063:         original numeric format. This function correctly includes the percentage symbol if present.
L00064:         """
L00065:         number_pattern = r'\b\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\b(?:\.\d+)?%?|\b\d+\b(?:\.\d+)?%?'
L00066:         matches = regex.findall(number_pattern, input_string)
L00067:         return matches
L00068: 
L00069:     def convert_to_float(value):
L00070:         """
L00071:         Convert string to float, removing commas and handling percentages if specified.
L00072:         Converts percentages by dividing the number by 100.
L00073:         """
L00074:         value = str(value).replace(',', '')  # Ensure value is treated as a string
L00075:         if '%' in value:
L00076:             value = value.replace('%', '')
L00077:             return float(value) / 100
L00078:         return float(value)
L00079:     
L00080:     
L00081:     def is_within_precision(converted_pred_numbers, gold_value, precision):
L00082:         """
L00083:         Checks if any number in converted_pred_numbers is within a specified precision of gold_value.
L00084:         """
L00085:         return any(abs(num - gold_value) <= 10 ** (-precision) for num in converted_pred_numbers)
L00086: 
L00087:     pred_numbers = extract_numbers(pred)
L00088: 
L00089: 
L00090:     if (isinstance(gold,(str,float)) or (isinstance(gold, list)  and len(gold)==1 )) and len(pred_numbers)!=1:
L00091:         return 0
L00092:     converted_pred_numbers = [convert_to_float(num) for num in pred_numbers]
L00093:     gold = [convert_to_float(g) for g in (gold if isinstance(gold, list) else [gold])]
L00094:     
L00095:     if percentage:
L00096:         gold = [y for x in gold for y in (x, x * 100)]
L00097: 
L00098:     if conj == "and":
L00099:         return 1 if all(is_within_precision(converted_pred_numbers, gold_value, precision) for gold_value in gold) else 0
L00100:     elif conj == "or":
L00101:         return 1 if any(is_within_precision(converted_pred_numbers, gold_value, precision) for gold_value in gold) else 0
L00102:     else:
L00103:         raise ValueError(f"Invalid value for 'conj'. Choose 'and' or 'or'. Received: {conj}")

L00109: def compare_pandas_table(pred, gold, condition_cols=[], ignore_order=False):
L00110:     
L00111:     tolerance = 1e-2
L00112: 
L00113:     def vectors_match(v1, v2, tol=tolerance, ignore_order_=False):
L00114:         try:
L00115:             if ignore_order_:
L00116:                 v1, v2 = (sorted(v1, key=lambda x: (x is None, str(x), isinstance(x, (int, float)))),
L00117:                         sorted(v2, key=lambda x: (x is None, str(x), isinstance(x, (int, float)))))
L00118:             if len(v1) != len(v2):
L00119:                 return False
L00120:             for a, b in zip(v1, v2):
L00121:                 if pd.isna(a) and pd.isna(b):
L00122:                     continue
L00123:                 elif isinstance(a, (int, float)) and isinstance(b, (int, float)):
L00124:                     if not math.isclose(float(a), float(b), abs_tol=tol):
L00125:                         return False
L00126:                 elif a != b:
L00127:                     return False
L00128:             return True
L00129:         except Exception as e:
L00130:             return False
L00131:     
L00132:     if condition_cols != []:
L00133:         gold_cols = gold.iloc[:, condition_cols]
L00134:     else:
L00135:         gold_cols = gold
L00136:     pred_cols = pred
L00137:     
L00138:     t_gold_list = gold_cols.transpose().values.tolist()
L00139:     t_pred_list = pred_cols.transpose().values.tolist()
L00140:     score = 1
L00141:     for _, gold in enumerate(t_gold_list):
L00142:         if not any(vectors_match(gold, pred, ignore_order_=ignore_order) for pred in t_pred_list):
L00143:             score = 0
L00144:         else:
L00145:             for j, pred in enumerate(t_pred_list):
L00146:                 if vectors_match(gold, pred, ignore_order_=ignore_order):
L00147:                     break
L00148: 
L00149:     return score

L00152: def compare_multi_pandas_table(pred, multi_gold, multi_condition_cols=[], multi_ignore_order=False):
L00153:     if multi_condition_cols == [] or multi_condition_cols == [[]] or multi_condition_cols == [None] or multi_condition_cols == None:
L00154:         multi_condition_cols = [[] for _ in range(len(multi_gold))]
L00155:     multi_ignore_order = [multi_ignore_order for _ in range(len(multi_gold))]

L00184: def duckdb_match(result: str, gold: str, condition_tabs=None, condition_cols: List[List[int]]=None, ignore_orders: List[bool]=None):
L00185:     """
L00186:     Parameters:
L00187:     - result (str): Path to the DuckDB file containing the result tables.
L00188:     - gold (str): Path to the DuckDB file containing the gold standard tables.
L00189:     - condition_tabs (List[str], optional): List of table names to be checked. If not provided, all tables in the gold DuckDB file will be considered.
L00190:     - condition_cols (List[List[int]], optional): A list of lists, where each inner list contains column indices used for matching conditions for the corresponding table. Defaults to considering all columns.
L00191:     - ignore_orders (List[bool], optional): A list of boolean values indicating whether to ignore the row order for each table comparison. Defaults to [False] for each table.
L00192:     """
L00193:    
L00194:    
L00195:     def get_duckdb_table_names(db: str) -> List[str]:
L00196:         """
L00197:         Retrieves the names of all tables in the DuckDB database.
L00198: 
L00199:         Parameters:
L00200:         - db (str): The path to the DuckDB database file.
L00201: 
L00202:         Returns:
L00203:         - List[str]: A list of table names in the DuckDB database.
L00204:         """
L00205:         con = duckdb.connect(database=db, read_only=True)
L00206:         result = con.execute("SHOW TABLES").fetchall()
L00207:         con.close()
L00208:         return [row[0] for row in result]

L00210:     
L00211:     def get_duckdb_pandas_table(db, table_name):
L00212:         con = duckdb.connect(database=db, read_only=True)
L00213:         df = con.execute(f'SELECT * FROM {table_name}').fetchdf()
L00214:         con.close()
L00215:         return df
L00216:     
L00217:     if condition_tabs is None:
L00218:         condition_tabs = get_duckdb_table_names(gold)
L00219: 
L00220:     gold_tables = [get_duckdb_pandas_table(gold, table_name) for table_name in condition_tabs]
L00221:     try:
L00222:         pred_tables = [get_duckdb_pandas_table(result, table_name) for table_name in condition_tabs]
L00223:     except:
L00224:         return 0
L00225:     
L00226:     assert len(gold_tables) == len(pred_tables)
L00227: 
L00228:     if ignore_orders is None:
L00229:         ignore_orders = [False] * len(gold_tables)
L00230:         
L00231:     assert len(ignore_orders) == len(gold_tables)
L00232: 
L00233:     if condition_cols is None:
L00234:         condition_cols = [[]] * len(gold_tables)
L00235: 
L00236: 
L00237:     assert len(condition_cols) == len(gold_tables)

L00239:     for i, (gold_table, pred_table) in enumerate(zip(gold_tables, pred_tables)):
L00240:         if not compare_pandas_table(pred_table, gold_table, condition_cols=condition_cols[i], ignore_order=ignore_orders[i]):
L00241:             return 0

L00243:     return 1
